headline: Italian Biomethane Plant Powers 3,200 Homes With Farm Waste
meta_description: A new biomethane facility in southern Italy converts agricultural waste into clean energy, powering thousands of homes while cutting CO2 emissions by 9,000 ton…
summary_short: Axpo's new biomethane plant in Grottole, Italy, now supplies renewable gas to over 3,200 households while transforming farm waste into low-carbon fuel.
body:
A biomethane plant that came online this July in Grottole, Italy, is now converting agricultural waste into renewable energy for thousands of homes while cutting carbon emissions significantly. Operated by Swiss-based energy developer Axpo, the facility will produce 45 gigawatt-hours of renewable gas annually—equivalent to the energy consumption of approximately 3,200 Italian households. By replacing natural gas with biomethane, the plant will prevent around 9,000 tons of direct CO2 emissions each year, while also generating valuable fertilizer from the processing byproducts. The plant is currently halfway through its six-month ramp-up phase following its July switchon.

Italy's embrace of biomethane represents a pragmatic solution to an energy puzzle: the country depends on natural gas for nearly half its electricity generation, yet produces almost none domestically. Rather than overhaul existing infrastructure, Italy is leveraging its extensive gas pipeline network to scale up biomethane production from agricultural byproducts. The strategy is working. The country's biomethane capacity has surged from 0.25 billion cubic meters in 2022 to a projected 1.6 billion cubic meters by 2026, positioning biofuels as Italy's largest domestic renewable energy source at 35% of the market.

The timing is particularly urgent as Europe faces tighter energy supplies heading into winter, with natural gas stockpiles at historic lows. Axpo, which operates similar facilities across Spain, Switzerland, and Poland, views Grottole as central to its renewable energy strategy. By transforming farm waste into usable fuel and fertilizer, the plant exemplifies how circular economy principles can simultaneously address energy security and climate goals.
quick_facts: Grottole plant came online in July 2024 in southern Italy
Prevents 9,000 tons of CO2 emissions annually
Uses agricultural waste as feedstock; creates fertilizer byproduct
Italy's biomethane capacity growing from 0.25 to 1.6 billion cubic meters by 2026
